facility_roles.quote: In collaboration with China, an air shower observation array is built at Yangbajing (4300m above sea level, 90.53 deg E,30.11 deg N) in Tibet, China to observe high-energy cosmic rays.

intervals.label: Tibet air-shower arrays (Tibet-I, -II, -III)
intervals.note: Start of the first (Tibet-I) array at Yangbajing. The 2002 text says that array ran three years before many scintillation counters were added (Tibet-II). The ICRR chronology dates the construction of the "air shower gamma ray detector in Tibet" to 1993 and its completion to 1997 (Heisei 5 and 9). No source read reconciles the two.
intervals.quote: After three years of operation, starting in 1990, of the Tibet-I array

intervals.label: Tibet-III array
intervals.quote: The Tibet-III air shower array, consisting of 533 scintillation detectors, has been operating successfully at Yangbajing in Tibet, China since 1999.

intervals.label: air-shower array with underground muon detectors
intervals.note: The underground water-Cherenkov muon-detector (MD) array, about 3,400 m2, beneath the air-shower array; a 100 m2 prototype was built in 2007. Allows hadron rejection above 100 TeV.

name: Tibet ASgamma
notes: Experiment start: the official ICRR page gives no date; the 2002 collaboration paper says the Tibet-I array began in 1990 and the 2008 paper that Tibet-III has operated since 1999. ICRR's chronology dates "construction of air shower gamma ray detector in Tibet" to 1993-1997.
Status "active" rests on the 2019 and 2021 collaboration papers; no later statement that data taking continues was read.
Shares the Yangbajing site with ARGO-YBJ.

physics_goals.quote: Search for high-energy gamma-ray (3 TeV) celestial point sources
physics_goals.value: Search for high-energy gamma-ray celestial point sources at about 3 TeV.

physics_goals.quote: Measurement of energy spectrum and chemical composition of very high-energy primary cosmic rays
physics_goals.value: Measure the energy spectrum and chemical composition of very-high-energy primary cosmic rays.

summary.plain: A field of scintillator detectors and an underground water pool of muon detectors on the Tibetan plateau, 4300 metres up. It detected the first photons above 100 TeV from the Crab Nebula and the first diffuse sub-PeV gamma rays from the Galactic disk.
summary.technical: Sino-Japanese air-shower array at Yangbajing (4300 m): about 600 scintillation counters over 65,700 m2 (mode energy about 3 TeV) plus an underground water-Cherenkov muon-detector array (3,400 m2) for gamma/hadron separation above 100 TeV. Results include the Crab Nebula above 100 TeV (5.6 sigma, 2019) and diffuse gamma rays at 100 TeV-1 PeV (2021).
